chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

I asked him about the udder (infaḥah) that is taken from a dead goat. He said: There is no objection to it. I said: The milk remains in the udder of the sheep after it has died. He said: There is no objection to it. I said: And the wool, the hair, the bones, the bones of the elephant, the skin, and the eggs that are taken from the hen (after it dies). He said: All of this is permissible.

key_terms.ضَرُع: The udder (specifically of a sheep or goat)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no objection to it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is milk in the udder of a dead animal permissible to use?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of *ma'khl* (dead animals) by distinguishing between the carcass itself and its naturally retained byproducts, ruling that milk, wool, bones, and eggs remain pure and permissible for use even after the animal's death. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for validating the consumption of dairy and the use of materials like leather and eggs from animals that died naturally or were not ritually slaughtered, provided no external impurity contaminated them. It highlights the practical distinction between the *jasad* (body) and its *akhlaq* (attributes/products) in determining ritual purity (*taharah*).
